semantic_correction.stem: An RN plans to complete a scheduled wound dressing change at 1400. At 1330, the unit becomes busy and the RN considers charting the dressing change as completed now to save time later. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Chart the dressing change now because it is scheduled and expected to be completed later, then edit the entry if the plan changes.
options.B: Perform the dressing change first, then document the assessment, care provided, and client response accurately and promptly in the record.
options.C: Record only that the dressing change was completed and omit the wound findings so the note remains brief and avoids unnecessary detail.
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to document the dressing change and rely on memory so all routine care can be entered at one time.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly requires the RN to enter computer documentation accurately, completely, and in a timely manner. Federal hospital record requirements at 42 CFR §482.24 require medical records to be accurately written and promptly completed and require entries to be complete, dated, timed, and authenticated by the person responsible for providing or evaluating the service. Open RN/NCBI nursing documentation guidance directly states that documentation should be completed accurately and timely after the task is performed and that care not yet completed must not be charted as completed. In this scenario, charting the 1400 dressing change at 1330 would record an intervention and findings that have not yet occurred. B therefore correctly performs the care first and then documents the relevant assessment, intervention, and response promptly and accurately. A is advance charting of unperformed care. C omits clinically relevant assessment information. D creates an avoidable delay and relies on memory rather than timely documentation. Therefore B is the uniquely best answer.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Document nursing care after it is actually performed and record relevant assessment findings, interventions, and client responses accurately and promptly rather than pre-charting expected care or delaying routine documentation unnecessarily.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0074 tests what clinical information belongs in the health record after a fall. V2-Q0373 tests medication reconciliation during transfer. V2-Q0473 tests response to a staff privacy breach. V2-Q0474 tests pre-charting versus accurate/timely documentation after care is actually performed.

option_audit.A: Plausible time-saving behavior but incorrect because it records a task as completed before it has occurred.
option_audit.B: Correct. It performs the intervention first and then documents relevant assessment, care, and response accurately and promptly.
option_audit.C: Plausible brevity strategy but omits relevant assessment data associated with the wound-care intervention.
option_audit.D: Plausible batching strategy but unnecessarily delays documentation and increases reliance on memory.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. B alone combines actual completion of care with accurate and prompt documentation. A pre-charts, C incompletely documents the clinical episode, and D delays routine documentation without a stated necessity.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. All four options are within eight characters and use parallel documentation strategies; the correct answer is not conspicuously longer.
